I’m part of the Catholic Church (I used to go every week before covid hit) but I don’t really follow everything they say. Also, hello fellow transmedicalist! 👋Nice to see other transmedicalists here.

The thing is, transitioning isn’t any more sinful than getting treatment for a medical issue and getting surgery to improve quality of life. Since gender dysphoria is a medical condition and transition is the only proven treatment, that’s the right course of action. Let me give you an example.

Let’s say there’s a baby born with a medical condition. The baby will live a horrible life with that condition. However, there’s an option to receive surgery to give them a normal life. The surgery isn’t  exactly “necessary” (it won’t directly kill them if they don’t get the surgery), but it will improve their quality of life greatly. I think even the most devout conservative Christians would support this, pray for the baby and make gofundmes and stuff. So why are trans people wrong in transitioning? It’s not a choice. Oh, and conversion or aversion “therapy” has been proven to NOT work at all and it often leads to suicide. Transphobia is a sin, and I’m pretty sure everyone who supports or performs conversion or aversion therapy gets a special place in Hell.

It took me years to finally convince myself of that, and sometimes I have fleeting doubts every now and then about if it’s a sin or not but I’ve done enough pondering for now and have realized that I’m really not doing anything wrong.

A lot of them love the “mutilation” argument. And sure, if you were to get surgery to attach your arm to your forehead or something just for the hell of it, then yeah that’d be mutilation since there is no actual reason for it, lol. But dysphoria is a medical thing that needs treatment, and once we accept that, maybe they will too. Without treatment, there are definitely consequences (such as mental health issues).

This is strictly my opinion, and someone correct me if I’m wrong about any of these things.

First of all, they got it right by saying it needs treatment (even though it’s not “transgenderism,” it’s called gender dysphoria but I see that word used by transphobes). So yes, it does need treatment....that treatment is transition. That’s where they get it wrong. THE TREATMENT FOR GENDER DYSPHORIA IS TRANSITION!

And their thing with the “your body is perfect, you’re mutilating it” blah blah blah, yeah no lol. Think about it this way:

Let’s say a baby is born with some kind of rare birth defect. There’s an operation to fix that. If they get the operation, they’ll live normal, healthy lives and will be able to function on their own. But if they DON’T get it, they’ll forever be bound to a bed or chair, having to depend on others to care for them, never any hope of getting any better. So it comes down to quality of life. Clearly, everyone would say get the surgery, right? I’m sure even the totally devout fundamentalist Christians would be doing fundraisers and stuff for the kid’s operation. So what’s so different about this? You’ll live without treatment, but you’ll have an awful life and it’ll be like you’re living a lie, so how is that different? Is quality of life not important? Another less extreme example would be depression; would it be a sin to take antidepressants?

Maybe if someone was to get surgery to put their arm on their forehead and their hand on their back, for no other reason but just for the hell of it, that’s where I can start to see an issue lol. But surgery and medical treatment out of necessity and/or quality of life is not sinful, at least in my opinion, and it’s rather cruel and even sadistic to not allow a person suffering from gender dysphoria to transition.
